paper.title: On Generation in Metric Spaces
paper.summary: Extends language generation to separable metric spaces using scale-sensitive novelty and closure dimension, characterizes uniform and non-uniform generation, studies doubling-space invariance and metric dependence, and relates the metric framework to earlier discrete generation.

formalization_scope.summary: The valid semantic conclusions in Corollaries 3.2 and 3.4, Theorem 3.6, Theorems 4.1--4.2, Corollary 4.3, Example 4.5, Theorems 4.6--4.7 and 4.10, and Proposition D.1 are kernel-checked. Theorem 3.1 and Theorem 3.3 have full valid directions plus corrected necessity statements and counterexamples to their unqualified ambient-center converses; Theorem 3.5 is refuted; Theorem 4.4 has a proof diagnostic and a bi-Lipschitz replacement. Examples 4.8, 4.9, and 4.11 remain incomplete.
specializations: Closed-neighbourhood membership uses an order characterization of the source's infimum inequality, avoiding an extended-real representation while retaining closed-infimum semantics.
The metric is usually an explicit real-valued distance kernel, and each theorem exposes only the metric laws used by its proof.
Theorem 3.6 transports the P10 discrete union-separation witnesses through a classically chosen separated packing; no computability of the coding is claimed.
Proposition D.1 compares the metric semantics with P02's earlier discrete semantics at scales in the interval from zero inclusive to one exclusive.
The formalization is deterministic, semantic, and generally classical; it claims no extracted implementation or runtime bound.
gaps: The printed necessity directions of Theorems 3.1 and 3.3 are false under ambient-center covers without the internalization premises exposed by Lean.
Printed Theorem 3.5 is false under its stated finite-union hypotheses; Lean provides an explicit separable metric counterexample.
The fixed-radius finite-cover inference used by the proof of Theorem 4.4 is false. The full topological-equivalence theorem remains unresolved, while a mutual-Lipschitz replacement is proved.
Example 4.8's two negative regimes remain open because the printed infinite-row lemma does not guarantee that revealed row points belong to the target.
All four regimes of Example 4.9 and the equivalent-metric separation of Example 4.11 remain open.
No independent human source-correspondence audit is claimed.

claims.title: Uniform metric generation and finite scale-closure dimension
claims.statement_summary: Uniform generation at two novelty scales is characterized by finite scale-closure dimension for a uniformly unbounded-support class.

source_assessment.notes: Under Definition 2.2's ambient-center covers, the necessity direction inserts cover centers into a positive sample even though those centers need not lie in the covered common core. Lean gives a genuine-metric finite-class counterexample.

formalization.notes: The sufficiency direction is full. Lean proves a corrected necessity theorem under same-radius cover internalization and refutes the unqualified printed converse.

components.summary: Finite metric scale-closure dimension implies uniform generation.
Uniform generation implies finite metric scale-closure dimension under the source's unqualified ambient-center definition.

lean_links.notes: The proof needs only reflexivity and nonnegativity of the adversary scale once finite dimension is supplied.
The missing same-radius internal-center premise is explicit.
The finite class is UUS and uniformly generatable but has infinite scale-closure dimension.

audit_refs.scope: Generated audits for the Theorem 3.1 sufficiency, corrected necessity, and counterexample endpoints.

claims.title: Finite and countable metric classes are generatable at ordered scales
claims.statement_summary: Finite UUS classes are uniformly generatable and countable UUS classes are non-uniformly generatable when the generator novelty scale does not exceed the adversary scale.

source_assessment.notes: The conclusions are valid. Corollary 3.2's printed exact-maximum argument is replaced by a finite upper bound, and Corollary 3.4's enumeration is intersected with the target class to handle finite and empty countable classes.

formalization.notes: Both source-facing conclusions retain the printed hypotheses while using repaired proofs.

lean_links.notes: The repaired argument needs only a uniform finite upper bound, not the source's invalid exact maximum.
Finite-prefix subclasses are intersected back with the target class.

audit_refs.scope: Generated audits for the Corollary 3.2 and 3.4 Results endpoints.

claims.title: Non-uniform metric generation and nondecreasing covers
claims.statement_summary: Non-uniform metric generation is characterized by a nondecreasing cover whose subclasses have finite scale-closure dimension.

source_assessment.notes: The finite-scale-closure converse inherits Theorem 3.1's ambient-center defect. Lean gives a separable countable metric counterexample to the unqualified reverse implication.

formalization.notes: The exact uniformly-generatable-cover equivalence and the printed finite-dimension sufficiency direction are full. The reverse finite-dimension direction is corrected under internalization and refuted as printed.

components.summary: A nondecreasing cover by finite scale-closure-dimension subclasses implies non-uniform generation.
Non-uniform generation implies an unqualified nondecreasing cover by finite scale-closure-dimension subclasses.

lean_links.notes: This exact semantic equivalence is independent of the defective scale-closure necessity step.
This is the literal valid direction of the printed theorem.
The required internalization premise is explicit for every subclass.
The counterexample class is uncountable while every finite-dimension subclass is forced to be a singleton.

audit_refs.scope: Generated audits for the Theorem 3.3 semantic core, valid direction, repair, and counterexample.

claims.title: Finite unions of finite scale-closure classes
claims.statement_summary: A finite union of classes with finite scale-closure dimension is generatable in the limit.

source_assessment.notes: An explicit two-member separable weighted-star class satisfies the stated hypotheses but admits one presentation for which no generator can eventually be correct for both targets.

formalization.notes: The literal theorem is refuted rather than formalized. The valid general union separation is registered separately as Theorem 3.6.

lean_links.notes: The shared core is covered only as an infinite-range infimum condition and not by any finite prefix.

audit_refs.scope: Generated audit for the Theorem 3.5 counterexample endpoint.

claims.title: Uniform and non-uniform classes whose union is not limit-generatable
claims.statement_summary: Every metric space with infinite radius-r covering number contains a uniformly generatable class and a non-uniformly generatable class whose union is not generatable in the limit at scales at most r over two.

source_assessment.notes: Lean makes the source's reduction to the earlier discrete union-separation theorem explicit.

formalization.notes: A greedy countable separated packing transports the P10 discrete witnesses and all three generation conclusions.

lean_links.notes: No effective packing or inverse-coding procedure is claimed.

audit_refs.scope: Generated audit for the Theorem 3.6 Results endpoint.

claims.title: Scale invariance in doubling and finite-dimensional spaces
claims.statement_summary: In doubling metric spaces, UUS and uniform and non-uniform generation are invariant over positive scales; finite-dimensional real normed spaces inherit the conclusion.

source_assessment.notes: The conclusions are valid. Lean repairs a mistyped scale pair, supplies the missing quantitative covering comparison and internalization argument, and proves the finite-dimensional doubling bridge.

formalization.notes: All three source conclusions are represented, with stronger helpers showing that the scale-invariance part does not require UUS once the doubling internalization proof is available.

lean_links.notes: The input UUS radius and target radius are both explicit and positive.
Quantitative doubling covers supply the internalization missing from the general Theorem 3.1 converse.
Lean proves doubling directly from compactness and bridges arbitrary scales through coordinatewise minima.

audit_refs.scope: Generated audits for Theorems 4.1--4.2 and Corollary 4.3.

claims.title: Generation invariance under equivalent metrics
claims.statement_summary: Equivalent metrics preserve UUS and uniform and non-uniform language generation.

source_assessment.notes: The printed proof incorrectly infers preservation of finite-cover status at one fixed numerical radius from topological equivalence. Lean refutes that inference but does not refute the full headline theorem.

formalization.notes: A complete mutual-Lipschitz replacement is proved, and the exact fixed-radius inference used by the source proof is refuted. Neither result is counted as coverage of the original topological-equivalence claim.

lean_links.notes: The two metrics induce the same discrete topology but differ on radius-one finite covers.
Mutual Lipschitz domination gives the quantitative ball inclusions needed by the semantics.

audit_refs.scope: Generated audits for the Theorem 4.4 proof diagnostic and mutual-Lipschitz repair.

claims.title: Monotonicity in adversary and generator novelty scales
claims.statement_summary: Limit generation is preserved when both scales decrease, while uniform and non-uniform generation are preserved when the adversary scale increases and the generator scale decreases.

source_assessment.notes: Lean preserves the source generators and thresholds and uses only closed-neighbourhood and covering-number monotonicity.

formalization.notes: The limit, uniform, and non-uniform clauses are all kernel-checked.

lean_links.notes: Both adversary and generator novelty scales decrease.
The adversary scale increases and the generator scale decreases.
Every target-dependent threshold is preserved.

claims.title: Generation transfer under one-sided metric domination
claims.statement_summary: If one metric is bounded above by a positive multiple of another, UUS and generation in the limit transfer with the corresponding inverse scale change.

source_assessment.notes: The order-theoretic closed-neighbourhood formulation handles the infimum boundary without assuming a nearest center.

formalization.notes: Both the UUS and generation-in-the-limit conclusions are exposed in one Results endpoint.

lean_links.notes: All radii are divided by the positive domination constant.

audit_refs.scope: Generated audit for the Theorem 4.10 Results endpoint.

claims.title: The discrete metric recovers the earlier generation framework
claims.statement_summary: For the zero-one discrete metric and scales below one, metric limit, uniform, and non-uniform generation coincide with the earlier countable-space notions.

source_assessment.notes: Lean proves the equivalences at both generator and existential class-property levels.

formalization.notes: The limit, uniform, and non-uniform existential generation notions all reduce exactly to the P02 definitions.

lean_links.notes: The two scale parameters lie in the half-open unit interval.
Metric covering number reduces to finite sample cardinality.
Target-dependent thresholds are preserved in both directions.
